title: Priority for Spanish nationals in housing
detail: Priority access to protected and social housing (*vivienda protegida*) and to rent aid only for Spanish nationals, and changing or repealing rules that stand in the way of "national priority" (*prioridad nacional*). The programme makes strict border control the premise of all housing policy.
c: Priority by nationality alone conflicts with art. 14 of the Constitution (equality), with EU law on long-term residents and with the ban on discriminating against EU citizens. Social housing is allocated by the regions. In our estimate, courts would strike such rules down.

title: Repeal the Housing Law, add tax breaks for long lets
detail: Repeal the Housing Law (*Ley de Vivienda*); tax incentives for long-term letting and deductions for Spanish tenants; regulation of tourist flats (*VUT*) and more inspections of illegal ones. Deduction amounts are not given.
c: Repeal is realistic together with PP. Deductions "for Spanish tenants" discriminate by nationality, which EU tax law does not allow.
pos: Tax incentives keep landlords in long-term rental.
neg: Without caps, tenants in stressed cities lose protection against rising rents; part of the deductions ends up in the rent.

title: Squatters out within 24 hours
detail: Clear occupied homes in under 24 hours and return them to the owner at once; free legal aid for victims; no taxes or utility bills during the occupation; tougher Criminal Code; tenants who stop paying (*inquiocupación*) treated as fraud.
c: 24 hours is incompatible with the inviolability of the home (art. 18.2 of the Constitution) and the right to a defence: at least a short court process is required. If the home has not yet become the squatter's dwelling, police can already act at once.

title: Higher purchase tax for non-EU buyers and funds
detail: A middle rate for purchases that add long-term rental supply, and a "deterrent" tax for buyers from outside the EU (*compradores no comunitarios*) and for speculative purchases by funds and companies. Revenue would fund aid to home buyers and protected housing. Rates are not given.
c: A tax on non-EU buyers is realistic (Canada goes further), but a "deterrent" tax on funds is hard to square with the free movement of capital in the EU.

s.t: Finance Canada, 4 Feb 2024: ban on foreign ownership of housing extended to 2027

title: *Autónomos*: zero contribution below the minimum wage
detail: A €0 social security fee (*cuota*) for self-employed people earning less than the minimum wage (*SMI*); above that, a progressive fee from €50 depending on income.
c: Similar to PP but broader: zero for everyone below the SMI, which means lost social security revenue and an incentive for bogus self-employment. Doable by law, but costly.
pos: Easier for people on low incomes to start a business and leave the informal economy.
neg: Fewer contributions mean smaller future pensions for the self-employed, a hole in social security finances and an incentive for "false self-employment".

title: Tax on money foreigners send abroad
detail: A tax on remittances (*remesas*), so money earned in Spain improves the economy and services for people who live here. No rate is given.
c: A tax on transfers abroad conflicts with the free movement of capital and payments in the EU. The US introduced a similar 1% tax in 2026, but the US is not bound by EU law.

title: Repeal the 2021 labour reform
detail: Repeal the Sánchez government's labour laws, which the programme says increased job insecurity, discouraged hiring and "dressed up" temporary-work figures. It does not say what would replace them.
c: The 2021 reform can be repealed by law. But it is tied to EU recovery funds, and the temporary-contract rate fell from 25.4% (end of 2021) to 15.1% (end of 2025). Repeal would mean conflict with the EU and the unions.
pos: Employers get more flexibility in hiring; seasonal sectors no longer need to use *fijos discontinuos* (permanent seasonal) contracts.
neg: After the 2021 reform the temporary-contract rate fell (EPA: 25.4% at end-2021, 15.1% at end-2025), though critics say part of the drop is a shift to *fijos discontinuos*. Repeal would bring back more temporary contracts, plus conflict with unions and the NextGenerationEU commitments.

s.t: Labour Ministry: EPA analysis Q4 2025, temporary contracts 15.1%

title: End compulsory online appointments (*cita previa*)
detail: A right to be seen in person straight away at any state office, without booking an appointment online (*cita previa*).
c: Matches a PSOE promise; realistic in state offices, but it needs staff.
pos: Older people and those without internet get access to public services.
neg: Without extra staff, queues build up in offices.

title: Abolish *arraigo* and fast tracks to citizenship
detail: Abolish *arraigo* (residence based on settled ties) as a way of fighting irregular immigration, and scrap "fast tracks" (*pasarelas rápidas*) to citizenship.
c: *Arraigo* is set by law and regulation and can be abolished by organic law (176 votes, together with PP). The result: more people without status, working informally.
pos: Sends the signal that irregular entry does not lead to legal status.
neg: Hundreds of thousands of people would stay undocumented and in the shadow economy: less tax and fewer contributions, more exploitation, weaker integration.

title: Repatriation and "remigration"
detail: Repatriate people living in Spain irregularly (*repatriación*), and "remigration" (*remigración*): a plan to help foreigners leave who, in the programme's words, do not contribute or live on benefits. No mechanism is described.
c: Mass removal of irregular migrants is impossible without cooperation from countries of origin. "Remigration" of legal residents for claiming benefits conflicts with EU directives and the European Convention on Human Rights.

title: One health card valid across Spain
detail: A single health card (*tarjeta sanitaria única*) with a shared medical record nationwide; not knowing a regional language should not block access to health service jobs.
c: A single card is a long IT project with the regions. Dropping language requirements in public exams would cause conflict with Catalonia, the Basque Country and Galicia; courts have ruled differently on this.
pos: Patients get care in any region with a shared medical history.
neg: A large IT project; the language clause would cause conflict with Catalonia and the Basque Country.

title: End "health tourism"; irregular migrants out of the system
detail: End *turismo sanitario*; exclude irregular migrants from the health system except in serious emergencies (*urgencia grave*); audit the cost of immigration to the health service.
c: Excluding irregular migrants is possible by law (it applied in 2012–18), but many regions kept treating them then. In our estimate the savings are small, and non-urgent conditions turn into urgent, costly ones.

s.t: Real Decreto-ley 16/2012: restricted access to health care (BOE)
Real Decreto-ley 7/2018: universal access to the SNS restored (BOE)

title: Cut taxes on electricity
detail: A sharp cut in electricity taxes for households, businesses and industry, ending "double taxation" (*doble imposición*), plus a national energy sovereignty plan. Rates are not given.
c: Electricity taxes can be cut (as in 2021–23), but no rates are given. An EU directive sets minimum excise rates on energy.
pos: Cheaper electricity for households and industry.
neg: Lost revenue that funds the system; generators may capture part of the gain.

s.t: Real Decreto-ley 12/2021: suspension of the electricity generation tax (BOE)

title: Nuclear plan: keep plants open and build new ones
detail: Keep existing nuclear plants by scrapping the closure timetable (*calendario de cierre*), urgently study new reactors next to existing sites, and move viable projects forward as fast as possible.
c: Keeping plants open is realistic if the owners agree (see PP). New reactors, in our estimate, take 10–15 years and billions (France's Flamanville was connected to the grid only in December 2024); private firms will not build them without state guarantees.
neg: New reactors are expensive and, in our estimate, take 10–15 years to build; owners may not invest without subsidies.

s.t: EDF, 21 Dec 2024: Flamanville 3 reactor connected to the grid
